title: Sweet and Sour Pork
subtitle: Cantonese crispy pork with pineapple in a tangy glaze
excerpt: Sweet and sour pork (咕嚕肉, gu lu rou) is a Cantonese dish of crispy battered pork stir-fried with pineapple, peppers, and a tangy sweet-sour sauce of rice vinegar, sugar, and tomato. The batter keeps the pork crispy even after saucing if you add the pork to the sauce at the last moment.
sourceNotes: Sweet and sour pork is a Guangdong (Cantonese) dish that became the most internationally recognised Chinese restaurant dish in the 20th century. The gu lu rou version uses a light batter and a balanced tangy-sweet sauce. Many Western restaurant versions are too sweet and use a heavy batter; the Cantonese original is sharper and the coating is lighter.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead.

content.text: The key is timing: fry the pork in advance, let it rest, then stir-fry the vegetables and sauce, and add the pork to the sauce only in the final 30 seconds. This keeps the batter crispy. If the pork sits in the sauce it becomes soggy within minutes.

items.prepNote: 4 tbsp for batter, 2 tbsp for sauce slurry
fresh or tinned, cut into chunks
for deep-frying, or use a wok with 500 ml

content.text: Marinate the pork: toss with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and leave for 10 minutes. Make the batter: whisk 4 tablespoons cornflour with the beaten egg and 2 tablespoons water into a thick paste. Make the sauce: whisk together the rice vinegar, sugar, tomato puree, dark soy sauce, 2 tablespoons cornflour, and 100 ml water. Set aside.
Coat the pork pieces in the batter. Heat the oil to 180°C in a wok or saucepan. Fry the pork in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and cooked through. Drain on kitchen paper.

Pour off most of the oil, leaving 2 tablespoons. Stir-fry the onion and peppers over high heat for 2 minutes. Add the pineapple and toss for 1 minute. Pour in the sweet and sour sauce. Bring to the boil: it will thicken in 30 seconds.
Add the fried pork and toss briefly to coat. Serve immediately with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Batter is soggy when the pork is added to the sauce
items.cause: Pork was added too early or the sauce was too watery
items.fix: Add the pork to the sauce only in the final 30 seconds. The sauce should be thick enough to coat the pork rather than pool around it.
